claims.text: The target materials are coarse-grained or as-cast multiphase metallic alloys with unstable or heterogeneous phases.
A data-driven machine-learning model integrating processing data can precisely predict thermomechanical processing conditions.
The model can be used to tune thermomechanical processing conditions.
Machine-learning-guided tuning can simultaneously enhance phase stability, refine microstructure, and optimize properties in multiphase metallic alloys.
Processing variables used by the proposed model include strain, deformation temperature, strain rate, and cooling conditions.
The model can predict microstructure evolution and phase stability from processing datasets.
The proposed processing regime uses severe plastic deformation at moderate temperatures with controlled strain, deformation rate, and cooling.
Refined phase boundaries mediate phase stability and microstructure refinement.
Controlled precipitation structures mediate phase stability and microstructure refinement.
The predictive model captures nonlinear interactions among processing parameters.
Capturing these nonlinear interactions enables targeted processing adjustments.
Targeted processing adjustments induce beneficial precipitation and hierarchical microstructural features.
The induced precipitation and hierarchical features refine the microstructure without compromising phase stability.
Machine-learning-guided processing will produce a finer and more stable microstructure than conventional processing.
Machine-learning-guided processing will improve mechanical or functional performance relative to conventional processing.
Conventional alloying and traditional heat treatments do not provide independently tunable control over phase stability and microstructure refinement.
The success of the approach depends on the quality and representativeness of the processing datasets.
The complexity of multiphase systems may limit the approach.
The model may not fully capture all underlying microstructural mechanisms.
